import pandas as pd
import numpy as np

# Source file paths
source_files = [
    "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/intermediate_space/length1_93/training_0.csv"
]

# Target schema columns and types
target_columns = ['user_id', 'time', 'bet', 'win']
target_dtypes = {
    'user_id': str,
    'time': str,
    'bet': float,
    'win': float
}

# Load all source tables into a list of DataFrames
source_dfs = []
for file_path in source_files:
    # Read CSV with index_col=0 to ignore the first numerical index column
    df = pd.read_csv(file_path, index_col=0)
    
    # Ensure columns are exactly as expected in source schema
    # Source schema: ['user_id', 'time', 'bet', 'win']
    # Just in case, select only these columns (ignore any extra columns)
    df = df[['user_id', 'time', 'bet', 'win']]
    
    # Convert columns to target types where possible
    df['user_id'] = df['user_id'].astype(str)
    df['time'] = df['time'].astype(str)
    # For bet and win, convert to float, coercing errors to NaN
    df['bet'] = pd.to_numeric(df['bet'], errors='coerce')
    df['win'] = pd.to_numeric(df['win'], errors='coerce')
    
    source_dfs.append(df)

# Since there is only one source table and its schema matches the target schema exactly,
# the transformation is simply to union (here just one table) and output.

# Concatenate all source dataframes (union)
target_df = pd.concat(source_dfs, ignore_index=True)

# Reorder columns to match target schema exactly (should already match)
target_df = target_df[target_columns]

# Ensure dtypes match target schema
target_df = target_df.astype(target_dtypes)

# Write the result to the target path
output_path = "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length1_93/target_multisource.csv"
target_df.to_csv(output_path, index=False)
